newsitem.title: SWEDEN: INSTANT VIEW - Sweden cuts repo rate by 25 bps.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - Sweden cuts repo rate by 25 bps.

text.p: Following are analyst comments after Sweden's central bank, the Riksbank, cut its key repo rate by 25 basis points to 4.35 percent.
JAMES MCKAY, analyst at PaineWebber International
"Given most in the market had expected rates to have bottomed, this is clearly very good news for the short end of the curve.
"The Riksbank obviously feels -- rightly in our view -- that inflation poses little risk either now or in 1997.
"Rate cuts can be expected to continue, with the repo rate falling to 4.0 percent in Q1. Next focus will be the Riksbank's inflation report on due December 17."
BJORN ENGLUND, Swedish analyst at Unibank Markets
"The market would be looking for another repo rate cut on December 17, coinciding with the release of the Riksbank's inflationary report.
"There will be new speculation about further repo rate cuts because fundamentals show there's still potential for further monetary easing.
"As that one will keep steady for three weeks' time, I think there's potentitial...they could futher lower the repo rate.
"The fact that the Swedish crown held steady, actually gaining slightly after the repo tender, bode well for the Riksbank's move."
